en.title: Minimum Total Effort After Replacing Values With Existing Divisors
en.description:
In each step, choose two positions i and j; if the current effort[i] is divisible by the current effort[j], change effort[i] to effort[j]. You may do this any number of times, or not at all. The goal is to minimize the sum of the final array. The operation does not divide i by j; it replaces i directly with the current value of j.

The standard I/O, examples and editorial were written independently by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n and the second line contains effort. 1≤n≤200000, 1≤effort[i]≤200000.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: The answers are 17, 31 and 6 respectively. In the second example no value is divisible by any other, smaller original value, so values cannot simply become the common factor 1.
hints: Record the frequencies. Enumerate the numbers d present in the original array from smallest to largest, and mark with d every multiple of d that has not yet been assigned a smallest divisor; finally, sum each original value's frequency times its smallest present divisor.
